This cannot be undone. It erases the vault (passwords, private SSH keys, certificates, passphrases, sync secrets), the biometric keys of NextSH, the database (hosts, tunnels, keys, snippets, custom themes, enrolled devices, conflicts) and the known hosts list.

Before erasing, NextSH closes every terminal and SFTP browser, cancels the transfers in progress and stops the tunnels and the LAN sync. Commands still running in the terminals will be interrupted.

The app settings are kept. On the synced computer, remove this phone from the enrolled devices afterwards. You will then create a new vault.
To confirm the wipe, type the word “%1$s” exactly below.
Closing the sessions and wiping the vault…
Closing is not possible right now: NextSH cannot safely be reopened until this wipe is finished. Tap “Retry”. If this message comes back, restart your phone, then open NextSH again.
The wipe could not be completed: some data is still there. You can try again. If it fails again, close NextSH, open it again, then start over.

Choose a passphrase to encrypt the backup. It will be required to restore your data. You will then choose where to save the file.\n\nThe backup contains your hosts, tunnels, SSH keys, passwords, certificates, snippets, custom themes, known host fingerprints and some of your settings. The LAN sync secret and the security settings are never included.

Enter the passphrase used when exporting the backup.\n\nItems of the backup replace those on this device that have the same identifier. Known host fingerprints already on this device are kept. The backup can also approve servers: their fingerprints are added, except for a host already on this device, whose first connection will ask you to verify the server. Your security settings do not change. Items deleted since the backup was made will be restored too, and your other devices will receive them at the next sync.
